clue.text: Stirring up dirt is offensive

indicators.note: stirring something churns it about, so the letters of the two words that follow are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone muck-raking in the press is behaving offensively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' rearranges UP and DIRT together. The surface sense of stirring up trouble hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rotten and foul-smelling is offensive to the senses, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Very agreeable associate on a board

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another comes before it, so the friend sits above the rest

parts.note: a pal is a friend or associate
a table is a board, as in 'bed and board' or a festive board

explanation.surface: A colleague who sits on a company board is very easy to get on with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests a company's directors, but here it is a table, the old sense of board as a dining surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something palatable is pleasing to the taste or mind, hence highly agreeable.

clue.text: In the main this will make' a net gain

definitions.text: In the main this will make' a net gain

parts.words: In the main this will make' a net gain
parts.note: the main is the open sea, and a net gain is literally a haul landed in a fishing net by a boat working there

explanation.surface: A business that in general will turn a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as 'mostly' and 'net gain' as profit after costs; both are taken literally, the sea and a catch of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing boat dragging a net through the sea brings its catch up in that net.

clue.text: Travellers' accommodation accorded acclaim, for a change

parts.note: an inn gives lodging to travellers
an ovation is a burst of applause or acclaim

explanation.surface: A hotel won praise for doing something different.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovation is something newly introduced, a novelty or departure from the old way.

clue.text: Sailing vessel in which sherry may be served

definitions.text: in which sherry may be served

explanation.surface: Drinks are poured aboard a yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fore-and-aft rigged ship with two or more masts and a tall glass for sherry or beer.

clue.text: Panel showing caution about contact

indicators.note: about means one word goes round another, so care is wrapped around the contact word

parts.note: care is caution, as in 'take care'
touch is contact, as in 'keep in touch'

explanation.surface: A sign urges care around touching something.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartouche is an ornamental tablet or framed oval, as round pharaohs' names in hieroglyphs.

clue.text: Put out in a venomous temper

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies within the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown out during a spiteful outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters spanning the end of 'venomous' and the start of 'temper'.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone out of a job or place is to expel or eject them.

clue.text: Distinguished, though plainly incompetent.

explanation.surface: A celebrity who is nonetheless obviously useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plainly' asks for the second definition to be read as two plain words: incompetent means not able.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means eminent or worthy of remark, and split in two it says 'not able', unable to do the job.

clue.text: Nonsense written about very large perch

indicators.note: about tells us the rubbish word is placed round the size abbreviation

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: Rubbish is talked about an enormous fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' looks like the fish but is a bird's resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is where birds settle to sleep, a perch.

clue.text: A churchman's tots

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a churchman, and the 's gives a final S

explanation.surface: A clergyman's small children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tots' suggests toddlers, but it is the verb: to tot up is to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot is to total a column of figures, the same as summing them.

clue.text: Erudite King Edward

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king
Ned is a pet form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A scholarly monarch named Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's King Lear supplies the first part; the surface invites one of England's real King Edwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned (two syllables) describes a scholarly person with deep knowledge, a synonym of erudite.

clue.text: Its root can be used to make a savoury dish

indicators.note: the phrase says the letters of the first two words are material reworked into something new

explanation.surface: A root vegetable goes into a savoury meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be used to make' rearranges ITS ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock, a savoury course.

clue.text: A far-seeing invention

parts.note: split into Greek tele, far, and Latin-derived vision, seeing, the name of a device that shows distant scenes

explanation.surface: A visionary new device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far-seeing' sounds like foresight, but here it is literal: seeing at a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: The broadcasting set lets viewers watch events far away, which is what its Greek-Latin name says.

clue.text: Support a lay union

indicators.note: union says the letter and the wager word that follow are joined together side by side

parts.note: a lay is a wager, as in a bookmaker laying odds, so a bet

explanation.surface: Backing a trade union for ordinary members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay' looks like an adjective meaning non-clergy; it is a noun, a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage, especially in wrongdoing, so to give support.

clue.text: Popular change in the East over commitment — not heartless or unfeeling

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the coin sits above the bond word

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
a sen is a small coin of Japan and other Far Eastern countries, so loose change there
a tie is a bond or commitment

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word not is removed

explanation.surface: A fashionable reform out East goes beyond mere commitment, being cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the O from NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insentient means lacking sensation or consciousness, so incapable of feeling.

clue.text: Workers set about a renegade, resulting in reprimands

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the insects surround the traitor word

parts.note: worker bees, so workers are bees
a rat is a deserter or turncoat

explanation.surface: Staff attack a defector and are given a dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' reads as 'attacked'; it means 'placed around'.
explanation.definitionFit: To berate is to scold angrily, the same as to reprimand.

clue.text: Firm dates arranged quickly

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of dates are put into a new order

parts.note: fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A company fixes its appointments in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges DATES to STEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means resolute and unwavering, fixed in purpose, as firm is.

clue.text: "My soul hath her ____ so absolute" (Othello)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank: the missing word in Othello's line on reunion with Desdemona, meaning satisfaction or happiness

explanation.surface: A line quoted from Shakespeare's Othello with one word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Othello, landing in Cyprus to find Desdemona safe, says that if he died now he would be happiest, for his soul is so wholly satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means satisfaction or happiness, the state of being pleased with one's lot.

clue.text: The bursar should make a note in thanks more positive

indicators.note: in means the note goes inside the word for thanks

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
surer means more certain, more positive

explanation.surface: The college finance officer ought to write a more confident thank-you note.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is informal British for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A bursar manages an institution's money, the job of its treasurer.

clue.text: No longer quiet — learning to plumb

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
lore is learning or knowledge

explanation.surface: Someone, now noisy, is training as a plumber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plumb' suggests plumbing; it means to probe the depths.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb is to sound out or investigate thoroughly, as to examine depths.

clue.text: A leading churchman, being strait-laced, scoffed

parts.note: prim means prudish, strait-laced
scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: A senior cleric, prudish, sneered at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' looks like 'mocked'; it is British slang for ate.
explanation.definitionFit: A primate is an archbishop, the senior bishop of a country.

clue.text: Observes a metal container is an unlovely thing

parts.note: eyes is a verb here: watches, observes
ore is rock that contains metal

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a metal bin is ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a metal container' suggests a can or tin; it is ore, rock with metal inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at, a blot on the landscape.

clue.text: Kicking off in the break

explanation.surface: A football match restarts at half-time.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening means beginning, as kicking off starts a match, and an opening is also a gap or breach.

clue.text: The expedition set off

explanation.surface: The travelling party departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' reads as 'departed', but it is the other sense: to trip a switch or alarm is to set it off.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a journey or excursion, and to trip an alarm is to trigger it.

clue.text: Try a little discrimination

explanation.surface: Sample a bit of prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste is to sample a small amount, and taste is also discernment or refined judgment.

clue.text: A rod is sent for repair — expertise is called for

indicators.note: something sent for repair is reworked, so the letters of the first four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fishing rod goes to be fixed, needing a skilled hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for repair' rearranges A ROD IS SENT; 'is' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroitness is skill and dexterity, the same as expertise.

clue.text: None hurried to make port

parts.note: O is nought, none
ran means hurried

explanation.surface: Nobody rushed to reach the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: ORAN is a port in Algeria.
explanation.definitionFit: Oran is a major Mediterranean seaport in Algeria.

clue.text: Grim, causing many great displeasure

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, so a large number
ire is anger, great displeasure

explanation.surface: Bleak news upsets a lot of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' gives D, 500 in Roman numerals, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means dreadful or ominous, as grim does.

clue.text: The way a talking bird shows resilience

parts.note: St is street, a way
the mina or myna is a mimicking bird that can talk

explanation.surface: A parrot-like bird's manner shows toughness.
explanation.walkthrough: MINA is a variant spelling of myna, the talking starling.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the capacity to endure, close to resilience.

clue.text: Elite assembly in a river studio .

indicators.note: in places the shuffled word inside the letter a and the river abbreviation

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: assembly means putting parts together, so the letters of Elite are reassembled

explanation.surface: Top people gather at a riverside workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' reworks ELITE into TELIE, which 'in' puts inside A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop, a studio.

clue.text: People are kept in by sleet — bad weather conditions

indicators.note: the phrase says the people word is held inside the shuffled sleet
bad means the letters of sleet are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: Folk stay indoors because of foul sleety weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges SLEET to ELETS, and 'are kept in by' puts MEN inside it; 'bad' looks like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The elements are the forces of weather such as wind and rain.

clue.text: A veteran celebrity holding back say

indicators.note: holding means the celebrity word contains the next piece

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for say is read in reverse

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: An old hand who is famous keeps something in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns EG (say, for example) into GE, which STAR is 'holding'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is someone long experienced, a veteran.
